subject: Issue with standardization of the Measurment Model of lavaan

messages.author: 0010347e735c6d21
messages.subject: Issue with standardization of the Measurment Model of lavaan
parts:
Hi all,

I'm working on creating a small package that involves lavaan. I want the user to be able to read in a dataset as the input and let the package do the rest. Here is what the code looks like:

> library(lavaan)
>   
>   left.side <- paste("E", "=~")
>     right.side <- NULL
>   for(i in 1:nrow(cor(d))) {
+     if(i == nrow(cor(d))){
+       right.side[i] <- paste(colnames(d)[i])
+     } else {
+       right.side[i] <- paste(colnames(d)[i], "+")
+     }
+   }
>   model.1 <- cat(left.side, right.side)
E =~ E1 + E2 + E3 + E4 + E5 + E6 + E7 + E8 + E9 + E10

I want to use the result from above to generate the measurement model as coded below:


> model.1 <- '
+   # Measurement Model
+   cat(left.side, right.side)
+   '
>   fit.1 <- cfa(model.1, data=d, std.lv = TRUE)
Error in start.idx[i]:end.idx[i] : NA/NaN argument

However, the code errors out. Upon investigation the issue lies in the previous code that created model.1. When I run model.1 I get the following:

> model.1
[1] "\n  # Measurement Model\n  cat(left.side, right.side)\n  "

When I revise the measurement model to how lavaan was originally intended to be used the code works:

> model.1
[1] "\n  # Measurement Model\n  E =~ E1 + E2 + E3 + E4 + E5 + E6 + E7 + E8 + E9 + E10\n  "

In my mind, these two ways should produce the same result. Are there any solutions to this issue I am having? Perhaps an important change to lavaan is in order?

Thank you for your help.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Issue with standardization of the Measurment Model of lavaan
parts:
The model syntax in lavaan is a string literal. Hence the single quotes.
It is just flat text. It gets parsed by the
lavParseModelString() function (which is called by the lavaanify()
function). Of course, the syntax must obey some rules. The string
literal is assumed to contain formulas with operators like ~, ~~, or =~
and so on. If the string literal contains rubbish like the string:

cat(left.side, right.side)

then it is no surprise this it does not work. lavaan 0.6-1 will catch
this and give a more informative error.

What will work (and I believe this is what you intend to do) is this:

fit.1 <- sem(c(left.side, right.side), data=x, std.lv = TRUE)

or equivalently

model <- c(left.side, right.side)
it.1 <- sem(model, data=x, std.lv = TRUE)

So all you need to do is to construct the string literal using standard
R functions (you can also use paste, but not cat, as this just prints
the string to the screen). See the R documentation for character strings
for more information.

Yves.
